summary: Five direction samples written in tools/audio/synth/cat_pilot_energy.py, rendered with build.py (all five pass the general rules), spectrograms read, nine tests written and passing (thruster_c misses one number: attack above 1 kHz 41 % against 50 %, reported as targetsMet false). Numbers are shares of the whole-file plain FFT of the mono sum unless marked W (the Welch/Hann numbers that listen/measure.py prints, which differ a lot on short clips because the Hann window damps the first and last milliseconds). Where a brief number and the character disagreed I kept the character; the places are in 'unsure'. Nobody has heard these: all judgement is from numbers, spectrograms and CLAP.

sounds.layers: (1) opening click 2.2-6.2 kHz, 4.5 ms long, t60 6 ms, at 0 ms, 9 times the RMS of the jet (peak 0.27 against 0.21 for the jet, 1.9 dB above it). (2) jet from 2.5 to 204 ms: two noises with their own envelopes; high noise from 1.5 kHz up (weight 3-10 kHz, air to 16 kHz), swell 7 ms, a 0.9 pop at the start, fall over 42 ms; low-mid noise 250 Hz-2 kHz at 0.9 of the level of the high one, swell 16 ms, fall over 55 ms, 12 ms longer; both torn by a 25-130 Hz flutter (depth 0.38 and 0.3) and a 4-18 Hz wander (0.2). (3) closing click 1.8-5.2 kHz, 4 ms, t60 5 ms, 0.55 of the opening one, at 204 ms. (4) thin bleed hiss 2-12 kHz, t60 70 ms, from 204 ms, 0.30 of the jet. (5) thump from 206.5 ms: 150 Hz falling to 72 Hz (measured 128 Hz at 222 ms to 74 Hz at 326 ms), t60 130 ms, soft saturation, set so that it holds 17 % of the energy. Level: true peak -15.3 dBFS.
sounds.measured: above 1 kHz 74.5 % (target >=55), above 4 kHz 44.2 % (>=15), below 250 Hz 16.9 % (10-25); above 8 kHz 19.9 %; W: above 4 kHz about 36 %, below 500 Hz about 22 %. Jet above -20 dB from 0 to 210 ms. Strongest line about 11 % (W). -34.0 LUFS (mono) at peak -15.3. CLAP margin +0.037, best 'a short sharp burst of compressed gas from a nozzle'.
sounds.unsure: The Kenney references (5 s beds, 89-97 % below 250 Hz) only give a tilt: almost nothing between 500 Hz and 10 kHz and a hump at 12-16 kHz. I did not copy that (it would give a bare tsss with no body); the jet is broader, heavy at 1-10 kHz. If the owner wants it closer to the Kenney thrusters, move the weight up to 12-16 kHz and drop the low-mid noise. The first version had a click of 1 ms, 8 dB under the jet; I lengthened and raised it (1 ms band envelope of the first 14 ms above 2 kHz: 0, -9, -20, -30, -30, -22, -11, -8, -2 dB), so there is still a gap of about 30 dB for 2 ms between the click and the swell of the jet: the intended snap and then hiss, but it could sound like two events. Whether the jet is alive and not flat I cannot hear: the 25 ms envelope varies by 2-4 dB.

sounds.layers: (1) crack at 0 ms: 9 ms burst of 1.2-8 kHz noise (t60 5.5 ms), a 1.2 ms snap above 2.5 kHz at 0.8, a bounce knock 1.5-6.5 kHz at 7.5 ms at 0.45. (2) chesty punch from 1.5 ms: sine falling 330 Hz to 92 Hz (tau 50 ms, t60 190 ms) through tanh drive 2.2 and a 1.1 kHz low-pass, plus a second body 150 Hz falling to 58 Hz at 0.9, plus a short dull noise knock (0.22 of the punch); punch energy set to 1.75 times the crack's. (3) airy tail: 1.5-20 kHz noise (weight 3.5-12 kHz), bloom 12-40 ms, t60 270 ms, flutter 25-110 Hz, energy 0.6 times the crack's. Level: true peak -9.0 dBFS.
sounds.measured: attack (first 30 ms from onset, rectangular window) centroid 2823 Hz (>=2 kHz), 44.9 % of the attack above 1 kHz; below 500 Hz 52.3 % (W 42.0 %; target 40-60); above 1 kHz 46.6 % (>=25). Below 250 Hz 32.9 %, 125-250 Hz 21.1 %. Punch pitch measured falling from about 280 Hz to 71 Hz in 100 ms. -34.0 LUFS at peak -9.0. CLAP margin -0.033 (best negative 'someone tapping on a taut plastic foil'; an earlier version 'music').
sounds.unsure: CLAP does not like it (hint only). The attack centre reads 2.8 kHz with a rectangular window but only 0.64 kHz with a Hann window, so a checker that windows will call the attack dull; the crack is 9 ms long and the punch carries most of the 30 ms. The tail is mostly air above 8 kHz (44 % W) rather than 1-4 kHz. The peak (-9.0 dBFS) comes from matching loudness to A and C (see checks); the crack alone sets it. The 125-250 Hz octave holds 21 %, the zone of the plastic container, but the punch sweeps through it and 60-125 Hz holds 12 %, so I do not expect it to be boxy; I cannot hear.

sounds.layers: (1) solenoid clack at 0 ms: armature hit 2.3-5.2 kHz, 7 ms long, t60 4.5 ms; a second hit 2-4.6 kHz at 7.2 ms at 0.5 (4.5 ms long, t60 3 ms); housing knock 0.7-1.5 kHz, 9 ms, at 0.2. (2) thump from 4 ms with a 5 ms rise (one event): 132 Hz falling to 56 Hz (tau 40 ms), t60 130 ms, tanh drive 1.35, 420 Hz low-pass, energy 1.6 times that of the clack. No hiss. Level: true peak -9.3 dBFS.
sounds.measured: MISSED: attack above 1 kHz 41.3 % (target >=50). Met: below 250 Hz 61.3 % (>=60, narrow), 60-125 Hz 47.4 %, 125-250 Hz 13.7 %; above 1 kHz after the first 15 ms 0.8 % (<=10); low band 40 dB down at 100 ms (dies within 0.15 s); thump pitch about 112 Hz at 22 ms to 62 Hz at 113 ms (it starts near 130 Hz). -34.0 LUFS at peak -9.3. CLAP margin +0.102, best 'a solenoid valve clacking with a tight low thump'.
sounds.unsure: I chose character over the attack number. The two targets (half of the attack above 1 kHz, 60 % of the file below 250 Hz) pull against each other, because an exponential thump puts nearly all its energy into the first 30 ms. An earlier version met both (attack 50.8 %, below 250 Hz 62.2 %) only by starting the thump 12 ms after the clack with a 15 ms rise, so that the body peaked about 27 ms after the clack; the brief wants the body within a few ms and tight, so I moved the thump to 4 ms with a 5 ms rise and report the miss. A bigger clack (smaller THUMP_VS_CLACK) would lift the attack share but takes the file under 60 % below 250 Hz. The 125-250 Hz octave now holds 13.7 %. A short thump is one spectral line by nature (about 21 % in the 103 Hz peak, whole-file FFT; measure.py with its Hann window says far more because it hides the clack); I cannot hear whether it sounds like a bowl.

sounds.layers: (1) hiss and crackle of impact_shield_medium: same seeds ('impact_shield') and parameters (SHIELD['impact_shield_medium']), rendered for 1.4 s; crackle at 0.85 of the hiss in the first 150 ms. (2) growl in two channels: generator growl (100 Hz, odd harmonics, sag 0.2) in the middle, a second growl with another seed as side (above 200 Hz through mid_side, ratio 0.6), plus rough noise 600 Hz-2.2 kHz (independent left and right, torn by a 30-90 Hz flutter, t60 0.55 s); level 1.25 times the sparks over the first 0.5 s. (3) bass throb, mono, identical in both ears: four close pairs (56 Hz beat 8, 68 beat 9.5, 82 beat 7, 96 beat 6; second partner 0.45 of the first) plus a steady 66 Hz floor at 0.45; pitch sags 20 % at the hit (tau 0.22 s); one slow drift of +-5 % per pair; envelope 30 ms swell then -6*(t/0.62)^2 dB; tanh drive 2.2 for harmonics; the throb is set to hold 34 % of the energy. Soft limit at 3.2 x RMS of the first 150 ms, 250 ms fade out. Level: true peak -5 dBFS.
sounds.measured: below 250 Hz 56.6 % (>=30; W 67.4 %), 250 Hz-2 kHz 22.8 % (>=15; W 15.7 %, narrow), above 2 kHz 20.5 % (>=15; W 17.0 %). Throb band (<125 Hz): maximum at 100 ms, within 12 dB of it for 700 ms contiguous with 20 ms frames, within 12 dB until 0.95 s with 50 ms frames; last above -30 dB at 1.25 s, while the crackle band above 2 kHz is 30 dB down at 0.95 s, so the throb outlasts the crackle. Correlation L/R 0.596, below 150 Hz 0.9993, level difference 0.74 dB. -28.3 LUFS mono at peak -5. CLAP margin +0.065.
sounds.unsure: The 12 dB window is met with 20 ms or longer frames; with 10 ms frames the beat nulls of a 50-100 Hz band reach 23 dB because 10 ms is under one period of 50 Hz (a measuring effect, but a checker with 10 ms frames will fail it: contiguous time within 12 dB is only 330 ms with 10 ms frames). The beat is not a clean 6-12 Hz: the sag shrinks every partner distance by up to 20 % at the start and four pairs interfere; the dominant component of the beat envelope measured 12.9 Hz, a little above 12. The strongest spectral peak (W) is 31 % at 53 Hz (a +-14 Hz window; the throb is deliberately a bass band of 45-100 Hz, and the brief for A gave no peak limit): the struck-bowl risk, it may be heard as a standing hum. Isolated crackle bursts at 0.55 s and 0.98 s stand out in the spectrogram (the old hit does the same).

sounds.layers: (1) whoomp, mono (equal in both ears): sine falling 122 Hz to 42 Hz (tau 75 ms) with 3 % pitch wander, 9 ms swell, t60 0.8 s (7 dB down at 100 ms, passes 60 Hz about 90 ms in); a second sweep 260 Hz falling to 70 Hz (tau 90 ms) at 0.85 for the chest; rumble of noise 40-200 Hz at the level of the whoomp (12 ms swell, t60 0.55 s); no saturation (a clipped 30-40 Hz sine puts a hard line at three times its pitch, which showed up as a standing peak at 88 Hz). The layer holds 45 % of the energy. (2) sizzle: hiss_lr band centred 1.25 kHz plus 1.65 kHz sliding down (tau 0.35 s), width 0.85 octave, rho 0.5, flutter depth 0.5, double-slope decay, low-passed at 4.6 kHz; sparks (2-7 ms, 1.2-4.2 kHz, thinning) at only 0.06 of the sizzle. (3) field hum: five partials 183, 268, 337, 452, 617 Hz (levels 0.55-0.9), each a pair with a 2-7 Hz beat (partner 0.7), left and right detuned by 0.9 Hz, slow drift, bloom 10-140 ms, t60 1.5 s, amplitude torn at 3-14 Hz (depth 0.5); level 0.75 of the sizzle. Soft limit 6 x RMS. Level: true peak -7.2 dBFS.
sounds.measured: below 250 Hz 45.2 % (>=40; below 125 Hz 23.0 %, W below 60 Hz 3.7 %), 250 Hz-2 kHz 30.6 % (>=15), above 2 kHz 24.2 % (10-25, narrow), above 8 kHz 0.1 % (<=5), strongest spectral peak 11.2 % at 182 Hz (W; <=15; whole-file FFT 5.2 %); low band (<125 Hz) maximum at 20 ms (<=60). The 20-70 Hz band (20 ms frames) is within 8 dB of its top until about 0.2 s and within 15 dB until 0.35 s, and the spectrogram shows the low line lasting to about 0.8 s. Correlation 0.631, below 150 Hz 0.9998, level difference 0.00 dB. -28.3 LUFS mono at peak -7.2. CLAP margin -0.009 (hint only; best negative 'a cheap electronic beep').
sounds.unsure: An earlier version had 30 % pitch wander and a rumble twice as loud as the whoomp: it measured well but was a smear of noise with 1.3 % below 60 Hz (the 40 % below 250 Hz was carried by 125-250 Hz). I took that back: now a falling tone with 3 % wander and an equal rumble. A zero-crossing pitch track is useless on the mix of layers; the fall is shown by the spectrogram only. The 125-250 Hz octave still holds 22 %. Several numbers pass narrowly and moved by a point or two with every change (above 2 kHz 24.2 of 25; a re-seed would need re-tuning). The hum is five steady lines in the spectrogram (the level flickers, the pitch drifts little): it can sound like a synthesiser pad ('arcade video game sound effect' and 'cheap electronic beep' score near the top among the negatives; 'taut foil' scored highest with louder sparks). I picked the middle. I did not listen.

checks.name: build of the five ids
checks.result: all five pass the general rules (true peak, no clipping, DC, onset within 5 ms, silent last 10 ms); manifest validates. Final LEVELS (true peak dBFS): thruster_a -15.3, thruster_b -9.0, thruster_c -9.3, shield_a -5.0, shield_b -7.2.

checks.name: loudness inside the families (BS.1770 on the mono sum, clips under 400 ms repeated)
checks.result: thrusters -34.0 / -34.0 / -34.0 LUFS (mono sum, spread under 0.1 dB); shields -28.3 / -28.3 LUFS. The thruster peaks differ by 6 dB (A -15.3, B -9.0, C -9.3) because short low thumps count little in K-weighted loudness: the owner will hear A with smaller peaks. If he judges A too quiet or B and C too loud, move the peak targets, not the sounds.

checks.name: tests
checks.result: 9 tests, OK. The whole synth suite (discover -s tools/audio/synth/tests, 54 tests, including another agent's test_pilot_mech.py) passed once, OK. The README command with '-t tools/audio' fails here because the tests folder has no __init__.py (not my file, not changed).

checks.name: spectrograms read
checks.command: Read of the five PNGs in assets/audio/render/pilot/
checks.result: Looked at all five. A: hiss to 200 ms, then a thump with a falling line near 100 Hz. B: 100-300 Hz drop and an air hump above 5 kHz that fades by 0.2 s. C: a thump falling from about 100 Hz with a short bright mark at the start. The spectrogram window is 85 ms, so the first 37 ms and the clicks are not visible; the clicks were checked with 2 ms band envelopes. Shield A: broad 40-100 Hz bar for the whole file, crackle bursts decaying with a few strong isolated bursts later, thin growl lines at 250-900 Hz. Shield B (re-read after the whoomp was rebuilt): a falling low band 30-100 Hz that lasts to 0.8 s, body at 100-300 Hz, five hum lines, a sizzle that fades.

checks.name: CLAP (compare.py --spec, pilot negatives plus the global ones)
checks.result: margins: thruster_a +0.037, thruster_b -0.033 (best negative 'someone tapping on a taut plastic foil'), thruster_c +0.102, shield_a +0.065, shield_b -0.009 (best negative 'a cheap electronic beep'). CLAP is a hint only.

notVerified: Nothing was listened to. Whether any of the five sounds like the owner's plastic container, a submarine, a toy or a taut foil is a guess from numbers, pictures and CLAP.

Two definitions of share disagree on short clips: the plain FFT of the whole file (rules.py energy_share, used here) and measure.py's Welch spectrum with a Hann window, which damps the first and last milliseconds. I reported both where they differ; thruster_c, thruster_b and shield_a (250 Hz-2 kHz 15.7 % W) are the cases to watch. I do not know which one the reviewer uses.
The throb target within 12 dB for at least 0.4 s depends on the frame length (see shield_a); I used 20 ms and 50 ms frames, not 10 ms.
Whether thruster_c reads as one event (thump 4 ms after the clack) and whether the 30 dB gap after the opening click of thruster_a reads as a snap was not judged by ear.

describe.py (the describing model) was not run. The dither of the two-channel pilot files is not shared between channels (is_mid_side is false for path pilot); it is far below -80 dB and I only checked the 0.999 correlation below 150 Hz.

Another agent's tools/audio/synth/tests/test_pilot_mech.py was present and passed in the full run; I did not read it. build.py rewrote assets/audio/render/manifest.json on every run (normal build behaviour, but a shared file).
The rejected thruster_pulse_a render was not on disk and I never measured it; the model for the gas jet is only the two Kenney files.
After the last changes I re-ran the unit tests for this module (9 OK); the whole synth suite had passed earlier, before the final changes.
